items.claim: The row's one declared substrate signal is inverted at its own seams — the byte-true catchword adjacency lies on the opening seam it never argues, the closing seam its device_notes denies is genuinely empty, and the tov-comparative its own quoted bytes carry goes undeclared.
items.evidence: The row's quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.3.22, so engagement is met. I re-derived the shared-content-token adjacency sweep directly from the consonantal skeletons using the staged method (word-bound tokens, length>=2, function-word stoplist) and reproduced the staged per-chapter digits exactly (MT ch 4 = 4 shared pairs of 16), so the derivation is sound. Result: MT 3:21|3:22 SHARE two content tokens — הָאָדָ֔ם / הָאָדָם֙ and the interrogative in מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ (3:21, verse-initial) against כִּ֣י מִ֤י (3:22) — while MT 3:22|4:1 share ZERO. The row therefore declares catchword adjacency as its observed signal and then denies a nameable shared-root catchword at the seam where the sweep is in fact empty, while the byte-true adjacency, two consecutive rhetorical interrogatives inside MT ch 3's high-cohesion zone (15 of 21 adjacent pairs share at least one content token), straddles the opening seam undisclosed — the exact evidence for the rival the rejected alternative names (joining the animal comparison) but never weighs. Separately, MT 3:22 is a TRUE tov-min adjacency site: אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר — a tov token immediately followed by a genuinely comparative mem-word, one of 6 such verses book-wide — yet the tov-comparative signal is omitted here while the same signal is declared at MT 4:6 elsewhere in this cluster, where the adjacency is a false positive.

items.evidence: The quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.4.1. The shavti digit is exact at the named object and unit: the I-turned pivot token stands in 3 verses book-wide (MT 4:1, 4:7, 9:11). The closing-seam ground is byte-true — MT 4:4 opens וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי אֲנִ֜י, one of only 4 verse-initial waw-prefixed raiti openers among the 18 raiti observation verses. Internal cohesion is byte-confirmed twice over: MT 4:1 and MT 4:2 open the same waw+verb+first-person frame (וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ / וְשַׁבֵּ֧חַ אֲנִ֛י) and are one of only 4 shared-content-token adjacent pairs in MT ch 4 (all four re-derived: 4:1|4:2, 4:3|4:4, 4:7|4:8, 4:9|4:10); and tachat-hashemesh falls at MT 4:1 and MT 4:3, both INTERIOR to the span, with neither seam carrying it (ch-4 sites: 4:1, 4:3, 4:7, 4:15). The paseq at MT 4:1 is disclosed with the required single-witness, count-only hedge and no intra-verse position claim, matching the inventory. Cross-seam sweep of both boundaries: MT 3:22|4:1 shares zero content tokens; MT 4:3|4:4 shares exactly one, the definite noun הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה / הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה (word-bound in 6 verses book-wide: MT 2:17, 3:11, 3:17, 4:3, 4:4, 8:17), which I weighed and judge non-defeating against a full verse-initial raiti+first-person restart that also carries the hevel and reut-ruach verdict closing MT 4:4 — the shared noun's sense diverges across the seam (the evil deed done, versus the skill of the work).

items.claim: The row's stated bounding ground — third-person gnomic sayings on both flanks — is byte-false on the left, where MT 4:3 opens on an anaphoric 3mp suffix whose antecedent lies in the first-person MT 4:2, and the same seam carries the only cross-row catchword pair in the chapter, undisclosed.
items.evidence: The quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.4.4 and the reut-ruach digit is exact at the named object (the chasing-wind phrase in 7 verses, correctly held apart from the 2-verse rayon-ruach form). The defect is the stated seam ground. MT 4:3 opens וְטוֹב֙ מִשְּׁנֵיהֶ֔ם — the 3mp suffix on the second token has NO in-verse antecedent; it reaches back to the dead and the living of MT 4:2, which carries the explicit first person וְשַׁבֵּ֧חַ אֲנִ֛י. MT 4:3 therefore cannot bound this row as a self-standing third-person gnomic saying: at the bytes it is the dependent terminus of a first-person unit, which is exactly how the neighbouring span treats it — so the row's own two-sided form-shift ground holds on the right flank only. Second, the left seam is the ONE cross-row catchword-adjacent pair in MT ch 4. Re-deriving the staged shared-content-token method from the skeletons gives 4 shared pairs in ch 4 — MT 4:1|4:2, 4:3|4:4, 4:7|4:8, 4:9|4:10 — of which only 4:3|4:4 crosses a row boundary; the shared token is the definite הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה / הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה, word-bound in just 6 verses book-wide (MT 2:17, 3:11, 3:17, 4:3, 4:4, 8:17) with MT 4:3-4:4 its sole consecutive occurrence. Neither this row nor the span before it discloses it.

items.claim: The rejected alternative weighs the byte-EMPTY rival and never the byte-strong one — MT 4:4-4:6 as a single unit whose two flanking verses close on a byte-identical phrase that brackets this verse.
items.evidence: Every positive and negative byte claim in this row checks out, which is why the defect is confined to the rival chosen. Verified: MT 4:5 carries no first-person token (ch-4 first-person sites are MT 4:1, 4:2, 4:4, 4:7, 4:8), no hevel-family token (ch-4 hevel verses: MT 4:4, 4:7, 4:8, 4:16), and no tachat-hashemesh (ch-4 sites: MT 4:1, 4:3, 4:7, 4:15); and its no-shared-root claim against MT 4:6 is byte-CONFIRMED — the exact-token intersection AND the contiguous-substring intersection of the two skeletons are both empty, as is MT 4:4|4:5 apart from a stoplisted object marker. But MT 4:4 and MT 4:6 close on the BYTE-IDENTICAL two-token run וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ (verified equal byte-for-byte against וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ) and both carry the toil noun (עָמָ֗ל / עָמָ֖ל); their exact-token intersection is three content tokens, against zero for MT 4:5 with either neighbour. The strongest rival to isolating MT 4:5 is therefore that MT 4:4-4:6 is one bracketed unit with 4:5 as its embedded foil — a rival this row never states and never rebuts, having rebutted only the pairing with MT 4:6 that the bytes already rule out.

items.claim: The row propagates a tov-min adjacency false positive at MT 4:6 without the construction check that signal's own definition mandates, and rebuts the MT 4:4 rival on form alone while the byte-identical phrase binding 4:4 to 4:6 goes unnamed.
items.evidence: The quoted full-verse run re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.4.6, and the tov-opener digit is exact — MT 4:6 is one of the 12 verses whose first skeleton token is the tov adjective. The problem is the second tov signal the row declares. At MT 4:6 the token following the opening tov is ט֕וֹב מְלֹ֥א — that second token is the construct noun 'fullness', NOT a comparative mem-prefix; the actual comparative particle is מִמְּלֹ֥א, the FIFTH token of the verse. The staged signal's own definition flags this class explicitly (a mem-prefix after tov is not always comparative; a construction check is required before citation), and the row cites without performing it. The contrast inside this same cluster is exact: at MT 3:22 the adjacency אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר IS genuinely comparative and the signal goes undeclared there. Second, the rejected alternative (reading MT 4:6 as the conclusion of MT 4:4) is rebutted on formal grounds only, while its strongest evidence is never named: MT 4:4 and MT 4:6 close on the BYTE-IDENTICAL run וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ and both carry the toil noun עָמָ֖ל. Third, 'carries no first-person marker' is a universal negative shipped with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep, though it is byte-true (ch-4 first-person sites: MT 4:1, 4:2, 4:4, 4:7, 4:8).

items.claim: The ketiv/qere CONTENT claim is attributed to a count-only inventory that cannot carry it while the byte source that can goes unquoted, and the same-formula claim across MT 4:1 and 4:7 ships without its tier — the two runs are skeleton-identical but NOT byte-identical.
items.evidence: The quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.4.7, the shavti digit is exact (3 verses book-wide), and both the paseq and the K/Q at MT 4:8 are correctly disclosed against the inventories with the single-witness, count-only hedge. Two original-language defects. (1) The row states the VARIANT'S CONTENT — the eyes/eye number variant — as being carried by the staged mark inventory, but that inventory records the K/Q at MT 4:8 only as a bare count. The content is in fact byte-recoverable from the verse itself, which carries the unpointed ketiv inline before the pointed qere: עיניו עֵינ֖וֹ (plural ketiv, unpointed = skeleton grade; singular qere, pointed = byte grade). The claim is true, the named source cannot bear it, and the source that can is never quoted. (2) 'the same resumptive formula that opened 4:1' carries no tier. Spliced and compared: MT 4:1 וְשַׁ֣בְתִּֽי אֲנִ֗י וָאֶרְאֶה֙ against MT 4:7 וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה — these are NOT byte-identical (accentuation differs on both the turn-verb and the see-verb, and MT 4:1 carries an extra meteg); identity holds at SKELETON tier only, and the campaign's tier discipline requires that be named. Also unnamed: the row's closing seam is crossed by the rarest device in the stretch — the ordinal 'second' is word-bound in exactly 2 verses book-wide, MT 4:8 and MT 4:10, both inside the identical skeleton run of the not-a-second clause, so the device begun in this row's own last verse resurfaces two verses into the next row.

items.claim: The opening seam severs a book-wide-rare one/two device that is stated first in MT 4:8, the declared tov-opener signal does not instantiate at MT 4:9, and the unit_type deviation is argued from an English gloss with no Hebrew quoted and no tier.
items.evidence: The quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.4.9, and 'no first-person verb at all' across MT 4:9-4:12 is byte-true (the ch-4 first-person sites stop at MT 4:8; no raiti or amarti token in the span) — though it ships as a universal negative with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep. Three defects. (1) The declared tov-opener signal does not hold at MT 4:9: its first skeleton token is the PLURAL tov form in טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד, and MT 4:9 is in NEITHER staged tov set — not the 12 tov-opener verses (whose ch-4 members are MT 4:6 and MT 4:13, both belonging to other rows in this cluster) nor the 6 tov-min adjacency verses. (2) The one/two opposition the whole poem runs on is stated FIRST in MT 4:8: יֵ֣שׁ אֶחָד֩ וְאֵ֨ין שֵׁנִ֜י. Word-bound sweeps: the ordinal 'second' stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide — MT 4:8 and MT 4:10 — and BOTH carry the identical skeleton run of the not-a-second clause (וְאֵ֥ין שֵׁנִ֖י at MT 4:10); the 'one' token then runs unbroken across MT 4:8, 4:9, 4:10, 4:11, 4:12. A device this rare straddling the row's own opening seam argues continuity toward MT 4:7-4:8; the row cites MT 4:8 thematically but never names the shared bytes, and its strongest rejected alternative addresses only unit_type, leaving the actual boundary rival unengaged. (3) The wisdom_poem deviation rests on a 'tightly patterned three-fold anaphora (if...then)' — an English gloss with NO Hebrew quoted and no tier, and the bytes do not carry an anaphora: the three conditional clauses open on three DIFFERENT forms, כִּ֣י אִם at MT 4:10, גַּ֛ם אִם at MT 4:11, וְאִֽם at MT 4:12, with no repeated identical opener; and MT 4:10's causal particle subordinates it to MT 4:9 rather than making it a parallel member of a series.

items.claim: The rejected alternative's stated ground is byte-false: MT 4:15 opens with a bare ASYNDETIC first-person raiti — a stronger restart marker than either raiti form this same writer uses as a seam driver twice elsewhere in this cluster.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Eccl.4.13 and oshb:Eccl.4.16, and the rayon-ruach digit is exact at the named object (2 verses, MT 1:17 and MT 4:16, correctly held apart from the 7-verse reut-ruach form). But the row rejects a split at MT 4:14|4:15 on the ground that no first-person or discourse-restart marker separates them. MT 4:15 opens רָאִ֨יתִי֙ — verse-initial, first-person, and ASYNDETIC. Of the 18 raiti observation verses, exactly 4 open with the bare form (MT 1:14, 3:10, 4:15, 10:7) and exactly 4 with the waw-prefixed form (MT 2:13, 3:22, 4:4, 8:17), re-derived at skeleton tier from the verse-initial tokens. This same cluster treats the WAW-PREFIXED member as a seam driver twice — a fresh raiti formula at MT 3:22 (אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר follows it) and a fresh raiti verb opening the envy observation at MT 4:4 (וְרָאִ֨יתִֽי אֲנִ֜י) — so applied consistently the asyndetic member at MT 4:15 is the STRONGER restart, not an absent one. The row's own declared substrate signals include the raiti observation set, so the marker was registered and then denied in the same row. MT 4:15 additionally carries tachat-hashemesh — one of MT ch 4's 4 sites (4:1, 4:3, 4:7, 4:15) and a formula this row also declares — which reinforces MT 4:15 as an observation opener rather than a continuation of the MT 4:14 narration. The referential-ambiguity hold at MT 4:15 is honest and correctly registered; the boundary ground is not.
